items.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023
items.q: Because I played the way I played and I know the dude, that’s what Brubeck — wouldn’t want it any other way. You know I’m influenced by him naturally

ctx.x: But when it came time to the improvising?

I don’t think so. You know I’m thinking back at the beginning I know for sure you know now and for the last fifteen years, but I don’t think that was ever present. I don’t think I ever felt the need to, you know, I remember at the beginning there’d be some old curmudgeons coming up, “You’ve got some tough shoes to fill young man.” You know that kind of thing. And Dave and I joked about that because I told him that and he said, “Well I’m a 12-1/2, you’re 10-1/2 you know, yeah you do, you’ve got some big shoes —…

I think it’s interesting that the brothers — I don’t know whose decision this was, but their fourth player is not a saxophone player. Because I think that would have made even this question of trying to sound like Brubeck, even more pressing because then it looks like a real, like we’re trying to re-create —
